title: Awarded the National Natural Science Foundation of China Young Scientists Fund (C), project No. 52505044.
A paper on a multi-DOF serial–parallel robot for dynamic cervical traction was accepted by IEEE CASE 2026.
Our work on robot-assisted trunk control assessment after spinal cord injury was published in IEEE Transactions on Biomedical Engineering.
Student rehabilitation robot teams received national second prizes in the RoboCup China Open and iCAN Innovation and Entrepreneurship Competition.
The trunk rehabilitation robot has supported clinical studies involving more than 50 patients and was featured on CCTV-1 Evening News.
Four supervised undergraduate theses were recognized as Outstanding Undergraduate Graduation Theses by Zhengzhou University.
